correctness_confidence.basis: Rigorous machine-checked Lean 4 kernel with 0 sorry/warnings, covering prime-power polynomials, CRT factorization, and Fourier bounds, supported by exact-Q verifier passing all 60 adversarial red-team tests.

novelty.basis: Builds directly on recent theoretical advances by Osaki and Mori (2026), providing the first machine-checked algebraic kernel and exact-rational verification stack for these torus approximations.

reproducibility.basis: Fully reproducible via provided scripts, exact-Q datasets, and standalone Lean 4 proofs with zero external dependencies and explicit verification runs.

rigor.basis: Exhaustive formal verification across 18 Lean 4 theorems and 16 canonical exact-rational certificates verifying full-period [0, P-1] soundness and exact bit-exact calculations.

significance.basis: Establishes bulletproof verification for ACC0 circuit lower bound approximations, eliminating floating-point errors and closing potential loopholes in complex algebraic reduction pipelines.

strengths: Zero-dependency Lean 4 verification kernel with 0 sorry/warnings and explicit axiom footprint.
Pure-stdlib exact-Q verifier auditing full-period [0, P-1] soundness without floating-point arithmetic.
Comprehensive adversarial red-team suite with 60/60 forgeries rejected.
Clear scope calibration distinguishing universal Lean theorems from finite/periodic certificate audits.
strong_novelty_candidates: Zero-floating-point exact-rational verification stack for torus polynomial approximations and ACC0 circuit lower bounds
summary: This paper presents TORUS-ACC0-CERT-1.0 and a zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel verifying prime-power finite differences, Fourier rounding, CRT composite-modulus induction, and periodic-Fourier NMQC_oplus torus approximations from Osaki and Mori (2026). All 18 Lean theorems and 16 canonical exact-Q certificates pass rigorous automated checks.
weaknesses: Relies on external theoretical foundations from Osaki and Mori (2026) for overarching circuit complexity context.
Lean 4 kernel does not formalize general prime-power Lemma 9 for arbitrary (p, e, k) or probabilistic Hoeffding/Chernoff concentration bounds.
